{{Quote|It was at this moment that the Republic made what might now be considered a mistake: the Sith no longer posed a threat to the Republic, but the Supreme Chancellor was unsatisfied. Jedi and Republic forces were sent to Korriban and other Sith planets to ensure no remnants of the Sith Empire remained.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Gnost-Dural]]|<ref name="T12" />}}
Sometime after the [[second battle of Korriban]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] authorized a '''post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion''' of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] centered on the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]] of the [[Stygian Caldera]]<ref name="TEA" /> and outlying Sith colonial holdings elsewhere in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TCSWE299" /><ref name="TEA" />

This period of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] history immediately following the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]<ref name="T12" /><ref name="TEA" /> was characterized by internal civil conflict, rampant disease,<ref name="GH30" /> famine,<ref name="GH30" /> and ritual mass-suicides<ref name="TEA" /> among the surviving [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith-blooded]] remnant of the Empire. These events served as the backdrop to the joint [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]]-[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] counterinvasion of the Empire,<ref name="T11" /><ref name="T12" /><ref name="TEGtW" /> a campaign aimed at assuring the complete destruction of the Empire<ref name="SWTORE" /> and any vestigial threat it posed to the safety of the Republic.<ref name="SWTORE" />

Though some Sith survivors continued to oppose the Republic militarily,<ref name="GH30" /> most refugees fled into exile on outlying Sith colonies like [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], [[Thule/Legends|Thule]],<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="GatORW" /> [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], and [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]]<ref name="TEA" /> or joined the [[Sith exodus]] as members of [[Tenebrae|Vitiate's]] [[exile fleet]]<ref name="T11" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> bound for the forgotten colony of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].<ref name="GH32" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> In addition to these diasporas, a handful of vestigial [[Kissai]] and [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] communities persisted in isolation on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] well into the [[Old Sith Wars]] period.<ref name="KOTORCG" />

==Prelude==
===Golden Age of the Sith===
{{Main|Golden Age of the Sith}}
The [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] of antiquity was founded in [[6900 BBY]] by the [[Exiles]],<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> a group of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] survivors of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] who subsequently ruled and interbred with the primitive [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] native to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="GH23">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 23: The Sith Order Begins}}</ref> Over the next two millennia,<ref name="NEC" /> the half-breed descendants of this union came to rule the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]] of the [[Stygian Caldera]] and a handful of outlying colonies further afield,<ref name="TEA" /> remaining hidden in isolation for fear of discovery by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Around [[5100 BBY/Legends|5100 BBY]], a particularly powerful [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]]<ref name="JvS" /> by the name of [[Marka Ragnos]] overcame [[Simus|his rival]] in a [[Duel between Marka Ragnos and Simus|duel]] for the rulership of the Sith Empire.<ref name="TGAotS3:TFoaE">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> During his century-long tenure<ref name="GH25">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 25: Two Rivals}}</ref> as presiding ''[[Jen'ari]]'' or "[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]],"<ref name="TCSWE154">{{CSWECite|II|154|''Jen'ari''}}</ref> Ragnos oversaw a period of wealth and prosperity subsequently known as the [[Golden Age of the Sith]].<ref name="SWTORE" />

===Preparations for war===
[[File:Sadow_vs_Kressh.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The duel between [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] and [[Ludo Kressh]] occurred during the [[Funeral of Marka Ragnos]].]]
Ragnos died of old age in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]],<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> leaving a resultant power vacuum that was soon filled by contenders [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] and [[Ludo Kressh]].<ref name="GH25" /> Their [[Funeral of Marka Ragnos#Power vacuum|duel]] for the Dark Lordship<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TGAotS2:FfaDL">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> coincided with the capture of wayward explorers [[Gav Daragon|Gav]] and [[Jori Daragon]],<ref name="T12" /> siblings whose unexpected arrival to the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] on Korriban stoked fears across the Empire of Republic rediscovery.<ref name="NEC" /> Capitalizing upon such sentiments, Sadow orchestrated a series of events involving the Daragons that seemed to confirm the likelihood of an incoming Republic invasion.<ref name="TGAotS:PoaSL">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref><ref name="GH27">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 27: The Great Hyperspace War}}</ref> This power play ultimately allowed Sadow to portray himself as a potential savior of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] capable of answering to the Republic,<ref name="T12" /> empowering him to claim the title of Dark Lord of the Sith with the backing of a [[Sith Council]] majority.<ref name="NEC" />

As a noted imperialist possessed of expansionist sensibilities,<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TGAotS3:TFoaE" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="GH26">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 26: Naga Sadow's Deceptions}}</ref> Sadow was quick to use the alleged Republic invasion as an opportunity to push his own political agenda calling for the Empire to expand outward from its traditional holdings in the Stygian Caldera into new territories.<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TGAotS3:TFoaE" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="GH26" /> As the new Dark Lord of the Sith,<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TGAotS:PoaSL" /> he called for a preemptive invasion of the Republic and cobbled together an [[Sith invasion fleet|invasion fleet]]<ref name="T12" /><ref name="TEA" /> mustered around his fief world of [[Khar Delba]].<ref name="TGAotS:PoaSL" /> Though [[Ludo Kressh's faction|Kressh's faction]] discovered Sadow's deceptions,<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TGAotS:PoaSL" /> their attempts to address his treachery ended in defeat in the [[battle of Khar Delba]],<ref name="NEC" /> during which Sadow allowed Jori Daragon to escape the Empire aboard [[Starbreaker 12|her ship]].<ref name="TGAotS:TFotS12">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 5]]</ref> Sadow and his fleet followed the [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] secretly placed aboard her ship soon thereafter,<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="TFotSE:DM">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 1]]</ref> heralding the formal start to the Empire's lightning invasion of the Republic.<ref name="T12" /><ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TFotSE:DM" />

===Great Hyperspace War===
{{Main|Great Hyperspace War/Legends}}
Establishing his headquarters in the [[Primus Goluud system]],<ref name="SWTORE" /> Sadow bolstered the numbers and military strength of his invasion forces with illusions of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] cast from afar within his [[Sith Meditation Sphere]].<ref name="TFotSE:TDoW">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref><ref name="JvS" /> Though the Sith Empire initially enjoyed a series of victories against the unsuspecting Republic,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TFotSE:TDoW" /> their advance was halted and their momentum stalled once the forces of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] regrouped and reformed at [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]]. Betrayed and attacked by his remorseful [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] Gav Daragon,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="NEC" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]]</ref> Sadow's Force illusions disappeared from the battlefields of the war as his concentration wavered,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" /> revealing the true size of the Sith forces.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" /> The Republic and their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] defenders,<ref name="TEA" /> augmented by [[Koros fleet|Korosian]] forces under [[Teta/Legends|Empress Teta]], drove the Sith out of the Republic and back down the [[Daragon Trail]] to Korriban.<ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" />

Sadow and his tattered fleet arrived at the Sith homeworld<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="TCSWE227">{{CSWECite|II|227|Korriban}}</ref> to find that the Empire had been claimed by a resurgent Ludo Kressh in Sadow's absence.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" /> In the [[First battle of Korriban|subsequent battle]], Sadow finally brought an end to his long-term rival,<ref name="SWTORE" /> though at a great cost to the collective Sith forces of both sides.<ref name="T12" /><ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" /> The full extent of Daragon's betrayal became evident with the sudden arrival of a Republic-Korosian task force armed with the [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogation]] data Daragon had managed to provide Teta prior to his death.<ref name="TFotSE:TDoW" /><ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" /> In the resultant [[second battle of Korriban]], the remaining Sith suffered heavy casualties,<ref name="SWTORE" /> and Sadow fled in disgrace into exile on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]],<ref name="T12" /><ref name="JvS" /> leaving the Empire to its demise. After assuring the destruction of the Sith fleet, Teta and her allies departed Korriban in haste, having suffered enough casualties and lost enough ships at the hands of the Empire.<ref name="TFotSE:EoaE" />

==The counterinvasion==
===Republic occupation===
[[File:Senate_HSW.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] authorized a joint [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]]-[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] invasion of the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]].]]
In the aftermath of its decisive defeat, the shattered Sith Empire was wracked by intermittent internal conflict, famine, and disease<ref name="GH30" /> as it reverted to the state of warfare and barbarism in which the Dark Jedi Exiles had discovered it millennia before.<ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> The shame of defeat and the loss of two Dark Lords in quick succession seriously affected the morale of those Sith who survived the war and its aftermath, ultimately leading to ritualistic mass-suicides undertaken by the lower castes of Sith society.<ref name="TEA" />

As the Republic began to rebuild and recover from the Sith occupation of its core worlds, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] authorized a joint Jedi-Republic counterinvasion of the Sith Worlds aimed at assuring the complete destruction of the Empire<ref name="SWTORE" /> and any vestigial threat it posed to the safety of the Republic.<ref name="TEGtW" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> The Chancellor and his political allies framed this invasion as a battle against the institutions of the Empire rather than a war for the extermination of its citizenry, stating that such actions were necessary to free the Sith population from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-sided]] corruption under which it had suffered for centuries.<ref name="GH30" />

Across the Sith Worlds, [[Unidentified Koros system battleship|battleships]] and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] laid waste to Sith military complexes and centers of power while Republic strike teams on the ground captured Sith survivors and refugees en masse.<ref name="SWTORE" /> Though some groups of Sith survivors continued to resist the Republic occupation militarily,<ref name="GH30" /> the Jedi tended to avoid killing Sith &mdash;instead, adopting the practice implemented by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]], the Jedi chose to [[Wall of light|sever]] their respective connections to the Force.<ref name="TSW1:EotW">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]]</ref>

===Artifact purge===
While the Republic focused on eradicating vestigial military threats posed to the Republic, the Jedi turned to the destruction of recovered [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifacts]] and [[Sith scroll/Legends|Sith scrolls]] found in the tombs and sacred places of the Sith. Since such objects were either weapons of the dark side, or propagated Sith ideology and teachings,<ref name="JATM" /> groups of [[Jedi Shadow]]s scoured the Sith Worlds for them,<ref name="KOTORCG" /> overseeing their destruction<ref name="JATM" /> or recovering them for study by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]].<ref name="SWTORE" /> Despite the Order's comprehensive effort to wipe out all significant repositories of knowledge,<ref name="SWTORE" /> certain caches of artifacts and scrolls containing preserved Sith knowledge survived the Jedi purge and were subsequently rediscovered in the centuries that followed by various groups of dark-side adherents.<ref name="TotJC" />

During this time, a number of museum curators of the [[Galactic Museum/Legends|Galactic Museum]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] decried the destruction of Sith artifacts as an act of cultural desecration and demanded that such antiquities be surrendered to the museum for preservation and display. Eventually, the Jedi Order agreed to a compromise, permitting certain artifacts to be displayed in the Galactic Museum's [[Sith Hall]] provided all [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]] be handed over to the Jedi.<ref name="JATM" /> A number of these holocrons found their way into the [[Great Jedi Library/Legends|Great Jedi Library]] on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] following its construction. Among these, the [[Dark Holocron]] remained in the possession of the [[Keeper of Antiquities]], Odan-Urr, until his death a millennium later in the lead-up to the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]].<ref name="JvS" />

===Destruction of sacred sites===
[[File:2ndBattleofKorribanHW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Unidentified Koros system battleship|Republic battleships]] bombard the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]].]]
In addition to capturing survivors and destroying artifacts, the Jedi and the Republic concurrently oversaw a campaign to destroy Sith sacred sites rich in dark-side power and structures housing arcane Sith lore.<ref name="SWTORE" /> Structures damaged or destroyed during this campaign ranged from the burial grounds of the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] on Korriban<ref name="T11" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> to the monolithic statues and monuments depicting ancient Sith that lined the cliffs of [[Begeren]].<ref name="SotS">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 1: Shades of the Sith]]''</ref>

At some point during this period, a number of Jedi stumbled upon the [[Veeshas Tuwan]] on the world of [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]]. The Veeshas Tuwan, a city-sized [[library-temple]] located in Arkania's frozen wastes,<ref name="TCSWE299" /><ref name="TotJC" /> was widely considered the foremost repository of Sith artifacts and lore in the Sith Empire.<ref name="TCSWE299" /><ref name="TotJC" /><ref name="TWGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> The Jedi destroyed the complex<ref name="TotJC" /> and its artifacts, recovering only a few, since they feared that the knowledge kept in the library would facilitate the Sith's regain of power. Subsequent groups of Sith in later millennia decried the destruction of the Veeshas Tuwan as one of the worst losses suffered by the Sith in their entire history, as many priceless objects and writings of cultural significance were presumed lost during its destruction.<ref name="TCSWE299" />

===Ritual of Nathema===
{{Main|Ritual of Nathema}}
During the last days of the Republic invasion, a reclusive Sith Lord named [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] emerged from the solitude in which he had spent the Great Hyperspace War and called a conclave of all surviving Sith Lords on his fief world of [[Nathema]].<ref name="GH31" /> Transmissions began blanketing the Sith Worlds with messages of hope,<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> warning listeners that the Jedi intended to [[Speciecide|systematically exterminate]] the entire Sith species and urging any surviving Sith Lords to join Vitiate in an involved [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual of Sith magic]] guaranteed to defeat the invaders.<ref name="GH31" /><ref name="TOR:Revan" />

Republic invasion forces assaulting Korriban were temporarily forced to retreat from the [[Horuset system]],<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="GH30" /> driven from Korriban courtesy of a [[Battle of Korriban (Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion)|suicide attack]] ordered by acting ''Jen'ari'' [[Shar Dakhan]].<ref name="TEA" /> In the brief lull that followed, Sith survivors tentatively crawled forth from the shattered tombs and ruined cities in which they had previously taken refuge.<ref name="GH30" /> Vitiate himself appeared in their midst in the days that followed and gathered to his side some eight thousand surviving Sith Lords<ref name="GH31" /> and Sith Councilors.<ref name="SWTORE" /> Returning to Nathema, these were joined soon thereafter by other Sith Lords from across the Empire who had likewise answered the call and converged on [[Vitiate's palace]] at his invitation.<ref name="GH31" /><ref name="TOR:Revan" />

Unbeknownst to those present, Vitiate had assembled the remaining Sith Lords for a more nefarious purpose than defeating the Republic&mdash;the assurance of [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]]<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> and the simultaneous elimination of any remaining potential rivals among the Sith.<ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="TOR:Revan" /> Binding the assembled Sith Lords and their respective power in the Force to his will by means of a potent ''[[Qâzoi Kyantuska]]'' invocation,<ref name="BoS" /> Vitiate undertook an extended immortality ritual that lasted ten days<ref name="TOR:Revan" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> and destroyed all life on Nathema.<ref name="TOR:Revan" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> The so-called [[Ritual of Nathema]] rendered Vitiate functionally immortal and granted him immense power in the Force at the expense of the planet and those in residence on its surface.<ref name="TOR:Revan" /><ref name="SWTORE" />

===Sith exodus===
{{Main|Sith exodus}}
[[File:Exile_fleet.png|thumb|right|250px|The [[Sith dreadnaught|Sith personnel carriers]] and [[Sith dreadnaught]]s of the [[exile fleet]] departed [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] on a twenty-year [[Sith exodus]] to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].]]
Having achieved immortality and overseen the destruction of any remaining potential rivals in the Sith establishment,<ref name="SWTORE" /> Vitiate departed his husk of a fiefdom with his loyal supporters in tow.<ref name="GH31" /> He publicly attributed the destruction of Nathema to the Jedi, using its desolation as further proof of his claim that the Republic counterinvasion was aimed at the systematic extermination of the Sith people.<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> Taking up the mantle of Sith Emperor<ref name="GH30" /> and promising revenge upon the Jedi and Republic, Vitiate cobbled together a [[Exile fleet|small fleet]] of [[Sith dreadnaught|Sith personnel carriers]] and [[Sith dreadnaught]]s<ref name="T11" /><ref name="T12" /> in preparation for a tactical retreat from the Stygian Caldera and Sith Worlds.<ref name="SWTORE" />

During this time, Vitiate once again presented himself on Korriban,<ref name="SWTORE" /> gathering the dispossessed and harried remnants of the Sith still in residence on the planet.<ref name="KOTORCG" /><ref name="SWTORE" /> Selecting from their number the youngest generation of survivors,<ref name="GH31" /> Vitiate and his fleet departed Korriban in haste to avoid attracting the attention of resurgent Republic forces rebounding from Darkhan's attacks. Over the next two decades,<ref name="SWTORE" /><ref name="GH32" /> the exodus fleet perambulated at random down the [[Kamat Krote]] in the general direction of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]],<ref name="SWTORE" /> a lost Sith colony world previously rediscovered by [[Unidentified Sith researcher|Vitiate's researchers]] prior to the Ritual of Nathema.<ref name="TOR:Revan" /> Over the years, the young Sith survivors came to depend solely on Vitiate for guidance and direction, listening with rapturous awe as he revealed his plans for a renewed Sith Empire capable of inviting vengeance upon the Jedi and Republic. The Sith dedicated themselves to training during their time adrift in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]],<ref name="SWTORE" /> arming themselves with the power of the dark side and analyzing the tactical and strategic circumstances that had led to their defeat in the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="SWTORE" />

==Aftermath==
===Survivors in the Sith Worlds===
The Jedi-Republic occupation forces temporarily forced out of the Horuset system<ref name="GH30" /> by Shar Dakhan's suicide attacks eventually returned to Korriban and successfully concluded the counterinvasion.<ref name="TEA" /> Though the Republic Military eventually withdrew from the Sith Worlds, Jedi Shadows continued to hunt down dark-sided artifacts<ref name="JATM" /> during the subsequent [[post-Manderon period]], though certain isolated caches escaped their notice and were eventually recovered by various groups of dark-side adherents.<ref name="TotJC" /> On Korriban itself, those Sith survivors who managed to evade capture by occupying Jedi-Republic forces<ref name="SWTORE" /> retreated into the planet's shattered tombs and remote deserts far from the major population centers,<ref name="GH30" /> forming vestigial communities of [[Kissai]] priests and [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors.<ref name="BoS" /> These communities and their respective settlements persisted in the more remote corners of Korriban for centuries, continuing to haunt the red wastes of their homeworld well into the [[Old Sith Wars]] and [[inter-Sith Wars period]].<ref name="KOTORCG" />

===Reconstituted Sith Empire===
{{Main|Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)}}
[[File:Vaiken_exodus.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The [[Sith exodus]] took the Sith across the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] and down the [[Kamat Krote]] to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]].]]
The Sith exodus fleet's twenty-year perambulations across the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]<ref name="TEA" /> came to an end around [[4980 BBY]] with the colonization of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]. Formally establishing a [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] under his control,<ref name="SWTORE" /> Vitiate set his people to work [[Dromund Kaas wilderness campaign|taming the wilderness]] of their new homeworld.<ref name="T11" /> He subsequently appointed new Sith Lords from among the population of young Sith,<ref name="GH31" /> the most powerful of whom served on the [[Dark Council]]<ref name="SWTORE" /> and oversaw the twelve [[Spheres of Influence]].<ref name="SWTORE" /> The Sith Emperor retreated into seclusion in the days that followed, leaving the day-to-day rulership of the Empire in the hands of his Council.<ref name="SWTORE" /> As the centuries progressed, the Empire continued to prepare itself for the day in which it would sally forth from its hidden refuge and take back the ancestral homeworlds of the Sith.<ref name="SWTORE" />

===Other Sith diasporas===
{{Main|Sith stealth regiment|Sorcerers of Tund/Legends}}
At the height of its power, the Sith Empire of antiquity oversaw and ruled some one hundred and twenty worlds<ref name="JvS" /> scattered across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. While most of these holdings were concentrated in the Sith Worlds of the Stygian Caldera, the Empire administered a number of outlying colonies situated in more distant sectors. Following the end of the Great Hyperspace War and the subsequent Republic counterinvasion of the Stygian Caldera, a number of Sith refugees fled to these disparate outlying colony worlds previously overseen by the Sith Empire.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="GatORW" /> Foremost among these Sith refuges were [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], [[Thule/Legends|Thule]],<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="GatORW" /> [[Tund/Legends|Tund]],, and [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]], though other Sith fled further afield into the depths of the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TEA" />

On Thule, a remote [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]]<ref name="GatORW" /> nestled outside the Caldera on its westernmost flanks,<ref name="TEA" /> a number of Sith loyalists joined themselves to a [[Sith stealth regiment]] headquartered on the planet. Confident that the Empire's defeat at the hands of the Republic would be temporary,<ref name="GatORW" /> this [[Special forces/Legends|special forces]] unit trained in preparation to serve as an advance force for the resurgent Sith Empire they predicted would eventually arise to avenge its defeat. While the Thule survivors remained in contact with other groups of survivors,<ref name="GatORW" /> their numbers depleted over the centuries, though their descendants continued to abide on Thule and serve the Sith even into the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]].<ref name="GatORW" />

Other Sith refugees fled to the distant planet of [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], a heavily [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Forceful]] world<ref name="KOTORCGWE5">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KOTORweben5|text=KOTOR Campaign Guide Web Enhancement 5: Karnak Tetsu, Sorcerer of Tund}}</ref> lost on the northeastern borders of the [[Open Sea/Legends|Open Sea]].<ref name="TEA" /> Originally the haunt of [[Kissai heretics|heretical Kissai priests]] who interpreted the death of [[Adas]] in the [[27,700 BBY]] [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[invasion of Korriban]]<ref name="JvSxviii">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], p. xviii</ref> as a sign to reject the dark side,<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> Tund was subsequently used as a Sith penal colony in the years prior to the arrival of the [[Exiles]] in [[6900 BBY]].<ref name="BoS" /> Over time, Sith refugees fleeing the Stygian Caldera merged with the native Sith abiding on Tund to form the [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]], a mystical group of Force users who resided on Tund until its destruction in [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] at the hands of [[Rokur Gepta]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Though several sources mentioning the counterinvasion seemingly consider it a part of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] itself, the vast majority suggest that it occurred after the formal conclusion of the war in the aftermath of the second battle of Korriban. The exact timeline of events constituting the counterinvasion is also never explicitly listed in any chronological order, though details can be pieced together from various sources. For example, the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic|''The Old Republic'' Codex]] entry titled "Galactic History 30: Rise of the Sith Emperor" mentions that Republic occupation forces were forced to retreat temporarily from the Horuset system for some unknown reason prior to the Ritual of Nathema. This was offhandedly corroborated by ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', with the reason for the Republic's temporary retreat revealed to be acting ''Jen'ari'' Shar Dakhan's suicide attacks on Republic forces sometime after Pultimo initially authorized the counterinvasion.

In [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 6]], Marka Ragnos is described as having been "the reigning Dark Lord of the Sith" during the Republic's invasion of the Sith Empire and is surrounded by ships flying as if in combat,<ref name="dlots6">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 6|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 6]]</ref> but [[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2]] begins with Marka Ragnos having died before the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire discover each other.<ref name="TGAotS2:FfaDL" />
